source_text: [1] Ἀπέχεσθε τῶν κακῶν βοτανῶν, ἅστινας οὐ γεωργεῖ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι αὐτοὺς φυτείαν πατρός: οὐχ ὅτι παῤ ὑμῖν μερισμὸν εὗρον, ἀλλ’ ὰποδιῡλισμόν. [2] ὅσοι γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου εἰσίν. καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μετανοήσαντες ἔλθωσιν ἐπὶ τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς ἐκκλησίας, καὶ οὗτοι θεοῦ ἔσονται, ἵνα ὦσιν κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ζῶντες. [3] μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου: εἴ τις σχίζοντι ἀκολουθεῖ. βασιλείαν θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομεῖ: εἴ τις ἐν ἀλλοτρίᾳ γνώμῃ περιπατεῖ, οὗτος τῷ πάθει οὐ συγκατατίθεται.
pass_a_gloss: Keep away from the evil weeds, which Jesus Christ does not cultivate, because they are not the Father's planting. Not that I found division among you, but rather a filtering out. For as many as belong to God and to Jesus Christ, these are with the bishop. And as many as repent and come into the unity of the church, these too will belong to God, so that they may be living according to Jesus Christ. Do not be deceived, my brothers: if anyone follows a schismatic, he does not inherit the kingdom of God. If anyone walks by an alien opinion, he does not agree with the passion.
pass_b_english: Stay clear of the bad weeds. Jesus Christ does not tend them, for they are not the Father's planting (Matthew 15:13). I do not say I found division among you. I found a sifting.
All who belong to God and to Jesus Christ are with the bishop. And all who repent and enter the unity of the church will belong to God as well, so that they live by Jesus Christ.
Make no mistake, my brothers: whoever follows a man who splits the church will not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:9–10). Whoever walks by a foreign mind does not consent to the Passion.

choices.why: A filtering out; the impure were strained off, which is why no division was found.

choices.english: a man who splits the church
choices.why: Participle of σχίζω; 'schismatic' is accurate but stiff in reading text.

choices.english: does not consent to the Passion
choices.why: Against those who deny Christ's real suffering; 'consent' keeps the verb's sense of assent.

anf_compare.notes: Minor. ANF 'exceeding purity' interprets ἀποδιϋλισμόν; the word means a filtering or straining out. Rest same sense.

bible_refs.note: φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου, the Father's planting

notes: Source shows 'ὰποδιῡλισμόν' with odd diacritics (for ἀποδιϋλισμόν) and 'παῤ' for παρ’; reproduced as supplied.
αὐτούς is masculine though βοτανῶν is feminine: the weeds are people.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] is the named Philadelphians 3 locus. Pass A keeps the clauses, including 'Not that I found division among you, but rather a filtering out' for 'οὐχ ὅτι παῤ ὑμῖν μερισμὸν εὗρον, ἀλλ’ ὰποδιῡλισμόν', 'Do not be deceived, my brothers' for 'μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου', and 'so that they may be living according to Jesus Christ' for 'ἵνα ὦσιν κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ζῶντες'. Pass B has 'I do not say I found division among you. I found a sifting.', 'Make no mistake, my brothers', and 'so that they live by Jesus Christ'. Citations (Matthew 15:13) and (1 Corinthians 6:9–10) match the supplied wording notes and are not wrong. Title 'The Father's Planting' names the thought. Odd diacritics on 'ὰποδιῡλισμόν' and 'παῤ' are disclosed.
reasons: Negation is moved onto a speech-act. Greek 'οὐχ ὅτι παῤ ὑμῖν μερισμὸν εὗρον, ἀλλ’ ὰποδιῡλισμόν' and Pass A 'Not that I found division among you, but rather a filtering out' deny the finding of division; Pass B adds 'I do not say I found division among you. I found a sifting.'

Agency of the warning changes. Greek 'μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου' and Pass A 'Do not be deceived, my brothers' keep passive deception; Pass B 'Make no mistake, my brothers' makes the brothers the agents of a mistake.

The conformity clause is not kept. Greek 'ἵνα ὦσιν κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ζῶντες' and Pass A 'so that they may be living according to Jesus Christ' are accordance with Christ; Pass B has 'so that they live by Jesus Christ'.

review.notes: Source paragraph 1: Locked Greek matches Ignatius Philadelphians 3. Pass A gloss preserves all clauses: 'Keep away from the evil weeds...' corresponds to Ἀπέχεσθε τῶν κακῶν βοτανῶν..., 'Not that I found division...' to οὐχ ὅτι παῤ ὑμῖν μερισμὸν εὗρον..., etc. Negation (οὐχ, οὐ) preserved in 'does not cultivate', 'he does not inherit', 'does not agree'. Agency clear: Jesus Christ as subject of cultivation, schismatic as subject of following, alien opinion walker as subject. Modality: indicative statements preserved. Doctrine: Father's planting, unity with bishop, repentance leading to belonging to God, kingdom inheritance denied to schismatics, assent to Passion preserved. Scripture: Pass B adds Matthew 15:13 correctly alongside 'Father's planting' (φυτείαν πατρός), and 1 Corinthians 6:9–10 alongside 'does not inherit the kingdom of God', matching the biblical allusions in notes. Title 'The Father's Planting' names the thought (φυτείαν πατρός). Notes disclose OCR issues: 'ὰποδιῡλισμόν' with odd diacritics and 'παῤ' for παρ’. No contradictions between Pass A and B; B adds scripture citations as required. All checks pass.
